item.title: [6.4] Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Tool-using voice agents often leave users waiting after speech ends, even when actionable information arrives earlier in the request. Speculative approaches begin work during speech, but chunk-bounded or interrupt-on-update generation can truncate a tool call before its arguments are complete. This couples computation time to speech updates, limiting useful work completed in advance.

WHY IT MATTERS

It presents a clever architectural improvement for real-time voice agents by decoupling speculative tool execution from speech updates using asynchronous 'Heartbeat Thinking'.

item.description:

Existing embodied-agent systems often focus on specified goals or abstract execution into symbolic actions, limiting evaluation in an evolving world. We introduce TARSphere, a robot-oriented full-stack framework for physically and socially grounded long-horizon embodied agents.
